specAnchors.text: understand that the genome is the entire DNA of an organism and that a gene is a section of a molecule of DNA that codes for a specific protein
understand that the nucleus of a cell contains chromosomes on which genes are located

primer.text: Zoom all the way out: the genome is the whole DNA library, a gene is one recipe inside it, and chromosomes are the bound volumes sitting in the nucleus — 23 pairs of them in every human body cell. This note pins those three levels together and adds the human genome project's map of where the genes sit.

modules.title: Genome and Genes
modules.opening: The genome collects all of an organism's DNA, and inside it a gene is a section coding for one protein, which is how genes steer characteristics: the proteins they specify — structural like collagen, or enzymes, or hormones — do the work of the cell.
keyPoints: The genome collects all of an organism's DNA.
A gene is a section of a DNA molecule coding for a specific protein.
Genes code for amino acid sequences that fold into proteins.
Structural proteins, enzymes and hormones are the taught protein types.
Characteristics are controlled because proteins direct what cells do.

low.restatement: The genome is the whole DNA library; each gene is one recipe in it.
low.analogy: A cookbook collection versus the single recipe that builds one dish.
low.examPointer: Name the three protein classes with collagen as the structural example.

medium.restatement: The causal chain runs gene to amino acid sequence to protein to cell function to characteristic.
medium.analogy: Blueprint to parts list to machine to what the factory can do.
medium.examPointer: Quote the chain when asked how genes control characteristics.

modules.title: Chromosomes in the Nucleus
modules.opening: Inside the nucleus the DNA supercoils into chromosomes, 23 matched pairs in an ordinary human body cell; genes occupy fixed locations along them, positions mapped in detail by the human genome project.
keyPoints: DNA supercoils to form chromosomes, visible during cell division.
Human body cells hold 23 pairs, 46 chromosomes in total.
The diploid number 2n reflects one chromosome per pair from each parent.
Matching chromosome partners are called homologous pairs.
The human genome project identified where genes sit on the chromosomes.

low.restatement: Chromosomes are packaged DNA, carried as 23 pairs in body cells.
low.analogy: Wool wound tightly onto spools so it stops tangling.
low.examPointer: Pair the numbers with the terms: 23 pairs, 46 total, 2n diploid.

medium.restatement: Each pair assembles at fertilisation from one maternal and one paternal chromosome, which is what homologous means.
medium.analogy: Two matched book volumes, one bought by each parent, shelved side by side.
medium.examPointer: Credit the human genome project for the gene locations.

glossary.definition: All of an organism's DNA, taken together.
A section of DNA coding for a specific protein.
A supercoiled structure of DNA visible during cell division.
Two matching chromosomes, one inherited from each parent.
